speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you have a history of chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to help me pinpoint the underlying cause, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do you notice any specific triggers like exercise or cold air?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

Your history of an 11-year chronic cough with thick, foul-smelling sputum, recurrent "bronchitis" infections, and morning exacerbations as a non-smoker is highly suggestive of bronchiectasis. To confirm this, I need to see your lung imaging and sputum analysis. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT. REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture. REQUEST TEST: FEV1_Spirometry.
